newsitem.title: USA: Vermont towns react differently on school funding.
newsitem.headline: Vermont towns react differently on school funding.

text.p: Controversy over how Vermont will pay for its schools cast a long shadow over town meetings, though lawmakers had urged towns to continue the current funding plans until a replacement system was in place.
In Burlington, the state's largest city, a tax increase to support the school budget was defeated by a two-to-one margin.
In Manchester, voters chose to delay the school budget vote until May, hoping that the legislature will have a new formula by then.
And in Stowe, residents voted to sue the state, if necessary, to stop any school funding plan that requires tax sharing among towns.
The State Supreme Court has ruled that use of local property taxes for school funding is unconstitutional.
